subject.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune

question: When all 512 SSH-verification cooldown entries are active, should the gateway retain the existing hard bound, reject admission of a newer cooldown, or intentionally allow temporary unbounded growth?
rationale: The requested behavior conflicts with the existing fixed-size cache invariant, and choosing which active cooldown loses protection (or whether memory may grow) is a gateway reliability policy decision.

options.title: Keep a hard cap with explicit admission policy
options.body: Preserve the 512-entry bound and define a bounded policy such as refusing a new cooldown while all retained entries remain active; add focused regression coverage.

options.title: Allow active overflow intentionally
options.body: Accept temporary growth beyond 512 only with an explicit owner decision, a documented maximum or rate-control strategy, and availability proof.

options.title: Retain oldest-entry eviction
options.body: Keep the existing bounded eviction semantics if the capacity invariant is more important than preserving every active cooldown.

recommendation.title: Keep a hard cap with explicit admission policy
recommendation.body: Preserve the 512-entry bound and define a bounded policy such as refusing a new cooldown while all retained entries remain active; add focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing candidate for the gateway reliability policy decision; direct feature-history verification was unavailable in the read-only sandbox.
